problems.title: Validity masks do not protect the full grounding path
problems.source_location: model/vision/basic_modules.py, AP, lines 69–122; model/vision/transformers.py, encoder forward, lines 197–215; pipeline/pipeline_mixin_old.py, lines 563–569
claim: One aggregation branch normalizes over padding; the encoder adapter discards its supplied padding mask; evaluation bypasses the grounding head’s object mask.
analysis: For valid feature \(u=(1,0)\), let \(X_A=(u,u,0,0)\), \(X_B=(u,u,10u,10u)\), both with length \(2\). Admissible zero projection/balance parameters give a masked first branch \(u\), unmasked second branches \(u/2,11u/2\), and final outputs \(3u/4,13u/4\). Only padding values changed, so pooling is not padding-invariant.

The encoder receives a key-padding argument but calls self attention without it. With identity projections, four valid \(u=(1,0)\) and four invalid values changing from zero to \(v=(0,1)\), active attention returns \(cu\) versus \(cu+(1-c)v\), where \(c\approx0.9012299943\); valid-key masking returns \(u\) in both cases. Finally logits \((0.6,0.4,1.2,0.1)\) with validity \((1,1,0,0)\) select padded index \(2\) unmasked versus real index \(0\) masked. These are admissible component examples, not measured checkpoint outputs.
result: Padding can change valid features and permit prediction of no real object along the active release path. Its frequency and effect on published accuracy remain unmeasured.
repair: For each nonempty valid set \(S\), normalize both pooling branches only over \(S\). Propagate and apply key-column validity before retention/softmax, and restrict final argmax to valid objects. Explicitly handle empty valid sets; a final mask alone does not undo earlier feature contamination.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The static path and exact witnesses establish mask-contract failures; no actual trained-model error rate or historical table lineage is supplied.

problems.title: The active retention levels differ from equal quantiles
problems.source_location: Section 4.3, p.6, Eqs.(4)–(5); model/vision/transformers.py, Attention, lines 70–122
claim: The paper describes \(L=6\) equal quantile segments with progressive retention. The six active code branches mix half/full counts with fractions based on eighths.
analysis: At \(n=24\), the paper’s retained counts are \((4,8,12,16,20,24)\); current active counts are \((12,24,9,12,15,18)\). Divisibility removes rounding as an explanation. Branches one and four are equal under strict ranking, so their contribution is \((\mu_1+\mu_4)A_1V\), leaving only five distinct levels. Two additional computed branches do not enter the output and cannot restore the stated family.
result: The release is not an exact implementation of the equal-six-quantile construction. Which schedule generated historical results and which is intended require clarification.
repair: Either document the actual fractions and duplicate level or implement the intended \(k_j=\lfloor jn/L\rfloor\), \(j=1,\ldots,L\), with positive-count and valid-key rules. Changing the schedule requires empirical re-evaluation.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This changes the released attention family, but the paper’s empirical advantage is not disproved by a source/specification mismatch alone.

problems.title: Grounding evaluation omits the last incomplete batch
problems.source_location: pipeline/pipeline_mixin_old.py, grounding evaluation, batch_size and num_batches around lines 518–536
claim: The grounding loop uses batch size \(3\) and floor division \(\lfloor N/3\rfloor\), although every query has already been encoded and no divisibility precondition is stated.
analysis: For \(N=5\), only indices \(0,1,2\) are processed. Outcomes \((1,1,1,0,0)\) give retained accuracy \(1\) versus complete accuracy \(3/5\); reversed outcomes give \(0\) versus \(2/5\). Thus the omitted tail can bias either way. For \(N<3\), no query is grounded and the later division has zero denominator. This is exact loop arithmetic, not a fresh neural evaluation.
result: The evaluator visits only \(N-(N\bmod3)\) queries. The actual omitted annotation list and its correctness require checkpoint-specific re-evaluation.
repair: Iterate starting indices \(0,3,6,\ldots<N\) and clamp each end to \(N\). Those disjoint intervals cover every index exactly once. Guard empty sets and absent subgroups before division.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a release evaluation-completeness defect; its possible metric change is bounded to omitted cases but actual historical impact is unknown.
